entries.t: Ivanti Connect Secure chain
entries.sum: Three flaws chained into root-level code execution on fully patched VPN gateways, without a login. The actor, tracked as UTA0576, left no malware or web shell. It re-exploited the device for every command and edited logs, which let it slip past Ivanti's integrity checker.
tl: First exploitation seen by Defused. Volexity dates the chain to at least 3 Oct.
Ivanti discloses. Two of three flaws patched.
CISA lists the remaining two and requires forensic triage.
entries.fix: Partly fixed on 13 Oct, with upgrade guidance for the full chain later. More than 5,500 gateways were exposed online.

entries.t: Plex2Shell
entries.sum: Four flaws chained into code execution on Plex Media Server. Not a zero-day: the fix shipped in August. Attacks began one day after details were published and installed crypto miners and proxies.
entries.fix: Victims were unpatched servers.

entries.t: Apache Roller: unauthenticated code execution
entries.sum: An unsafe deserialization flaw in the blog server's XML-RPC endpoint lets an attacker run code with no login, in every release from 4.0.0 to 6.1.4. Apache says it is being actively exploited. It is the same bug as CVE-2026-82384, which had listed only 6.1.5.
entries.how: A crafted request to /roller-services/xmlrpc, reachable even when XML-RPC is switched off in the admin screen. A proof of concept has been public since 28 September.
tl: Apache widens it to 4.0.0–6.1.4 and confirms exploitation.
entries.fix: Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later (6.1.7 recommended) or block the XML-RPC endpoint. Not yet on CISA's exploited list at the time of writing.

entries.t: Careers360: 3,609,421 accounts in a verified breach
entries.sum: In November 2026, data allegedly taken from the Indian education and careers platform Careers360 appeared on a public hacking forum . The 22M records included 3.6M unique email addresses alongside names, phone numbers, genders and caste categories, and most also contained students' entrance exam results, including ranks and marks. Data: Academic records, Castes, Email addresses, Genders, Names, Phone numbers.
entries.how: Not disclosed.
entries.fix: Under investigation.

entries.t: Too Lost: 724,323 accounts in a verified breach
entries.sum: In November 2026, an unauthorised party claimed to have obtained data from the music distributor for independent artists, Too Lost. The data contained 724k unique email addresses belonging to artists, their collaborators and fans. Some records also contained bcrypt password hashes, while a small subset included partial credit card data (last 4 digits and card type), identity… Data: Dates of birth, Driver's licenses, Email addresses, Government issued IDs, IP addresses, Names.
entries.how: Stolen or leaked credentials and keys.
entries.fix: Under investigation.
